sanskrit: nyamajjaṃs te mahārāja tasya kāye mahātmanaḥ yathā haṃsā mahārāja taḍāgaṃ prāpya bhārata
english: Those arrows sank into the body of that great-souled one, O great king, even as swans, O descendant of Bharata, plunge into a pond they have reached.

sanskrit: pīḍitaś caiva putras te pāṇḍavena mahātmanā hitvā pārthaṃ raṇe tūrṇaṃ bhīṣmasya ratham āśrayat agādhe majjatas tasya dvīpo bhīṣmo 'bhavat tadā
english: Hard pressed by the great-souled Pāṇḍava, your son left Pārtha in the battle and swiftly took refuge with Bhīṣma's chariot; and as he was sinking in those fathomless depths, Bhīṣma became his island.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ putras tava viśāṃ pate avārayat tataḥ śūro bhūya eva parākramī
english: Then, regaining his senses, your son, O lord of peoples, that valiant hero, once more held his ground and showed his prowess.

sanskrit: śaraiḥ suniśitaiḥ pārthaṃ yathā vṛtraḥ puraṃdaram nirbibheda mahāvīryo vivyathe naiva cārjunāt
english: With keenly whetted arrows that hero of great might pierced Pārtha, as Vṛtra once pierced Purandara, and he flinched not at all before Arjuna.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sātyakiṃ daṃśitaṃ yuddhe bhīṣmāyābhyudyataṃ tadā ārśyaśṛṅgir maheṣvāso vārayām āsa saṃyuge
english: Saṃjaya said: As mailed Sātyaki rose up in the battle against Bhīṣma, the son of Ṛśyaśṛṅga, that mighty archer, held him in check in the fray.

sanskrit: mādhavas tu susaṃkruddho rākṣasaṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ ājaghāna raṇe rājan prahasann iva bhārata
english: But Mādhava, greatly enraged, struck the rākṣasa in the battle with nine arrows, O king, as if smiling the while, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: tathaiva rākṣaso rājan mādhavaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ ardayām āsa rājendra saṃkruddhaḥ śinipuṃgavam
english: Likewise the rākṣasa, O king, in his fury tormented Mādhava, that bull of the Śini line, with sharpened arrows, O king of kings.

sanskrit: śaineyaḥ śarasaṃghaṃ tu preṣayām āsa saṃyuge rākṣasāya susaṃkruddho mādhavaḥ paravīrahā
english: Then the descendant of Śini, that Mādhava, slayer of enemy heroes, in great wrath sent forth a mass of arrows at the rākṣasa in the fray.

sanskrit: tato rakṣo mahābāhuṃ sātyakiṃ satyavikramam vivyādha viśikhais tīkṣṇaiḥ siṃhanādaṃ nanāda ca
english: Thereupon the rākṣasa pierced the mighty-armed Sātyaki of true valor with keen arrows, and roared aloud with a lion's roar.

sanskrit: mādhavas tu bhṛśaṃ viddho rākṣasena raṇe tadā dhairyam ālambya tejasvī jahāsa ca nanāda ca
english: But Mādhava, though sorely wounded by the rākṣasa in the battle, that glorious one, holding fast to his steadiness, both laughed and roared.

sanskrit: bhagadattas tataḥ kruddho mādhavaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ tāḍayām āsa samare tottrair iva mahāgajam
english: Then Bhagadatta, enraged, struck Mādhava in the battle with sharpened arrows, as one goads a great elephant with the spiked driving-hooks.

sanskrit: vihāya rākṣasaṃ yuddhe śaineyo rathināṃ varaḥ prāgjyotiṣāya cikṣepa śarān saṃnataparvaṇaḥ
english: Leaving the rākṣasa in the combat, the descendant of Śini, foremost of chariot-warriors, hurled smooth-jointed arrows at the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa.

sanskrit: tasya prāgjyotiṣo rājā mādhavasya mahad dhanuḥ ciccheda śitadhāreṇa bhallena kṛtahastavat
english: The king of Prāgjyotiṣa, with a sharp-edged broad-headed shaft, cut asunder the great bow of Mādhava, as one skilled of hand.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya vegavat paravīrahā bhagadattaṃ raṇe kruddho vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, taking up another swift bow, that slayer of enemy heroes, enraged, pierced Bhagadatta in the battle with sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho maheṣvāsaḥ sṛkkiṇī saṃlihan muhuḥ śaktiṃ kanakavaiḍūryabhūṣitām āyasīṃ dṛḍhām yamadaṇḍopamāṃ ghorāṃ prāhiṇot sātyakāya vai
english: That mighty archer, deeply wounded, licking the corners of his mouth again and again, hurled at Sātyaki a fearsome spear of iron, firm, adorned with gold and lapis, like unto the rod of Yama.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā tasya bāhor baleritām sātyakiḥ samare rājaṃs tridhā ciccheda sāyakaiḥ sā papāta tadā bhūmau maholkeva hataprabhā
english: As it came hurtling suddenly, sped by the strength of that arm, Sātyaki in the battle, O king, cut it into three with his arrows; and it fell then to the earth like a great meteor with its luster quenched.

sanskrit: śaktiṃ vinihatāṃ dṛṣṭvā putras tava viśāṃ pate mahatā rathavaṃśena vārayām āsa mādhavam
english: Seeing the spear struck down, your son, O lord of peoples, held Mādhava in check with a great host of chariots.

sanskrit: tathā parivṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā vārṣṇeyānāṃ mahāratham duryodhano bhṛśaṃ hṛṣṭo bhrātṝn sarvān uvāca ha
english: Seeing that great chariot-warrior of the Vṛṣṇis thus surrounded, Duryodhana, exceedingly pleased, spoke to all his brothers.

sanskrit: tathā kuruta kauravyā yathā vaḥ sātyako yudhi na jīvan pratiniryāti mahato 'smād rathavrajāt asmin hate hataṃ manye pāṇḍavānāṃ mahad balam
english: "Act so, O Kauravas, that Sātyaki shall not come forth alive from this great press of chariots; for once he is slain, I deem the mighty strength of the Pāṇḍavas slain."

sanskrit: tat tatheti vacas tasya parigṛhya mahārathāḥ śaineyaṃ yodhayām āsur bhīṣmasya pramukhe tadā
english: Accepting his word with "So be it," those great chariot-warriors then fell to fighting the descendant of Śini before the eyes of Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: abhimanyuṃ tadāyāntaṃ bhīṣmāyābhyudyataṃ mṛdhe kāmbojarājo balavān vārayām āsa saṃyuge
english: As Abhimanyu then came on, rising up against Bhīṣma in the fight, the mighty king of the Kāmbojas held him in check in the fray.

sanskrit: ārjunir nṛpatiṃ viddhvā śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ punar eva catuḥṣaṣṭyā rājan vivyādha taṃ nṛpam
english: Arjuna's son, having pierced the king with smooth-jointed arrows, struck that king once again, O king, with sixty-four shafts.

sanskrit: sudakṣiṇas tu samare kārṣṇiṃ vivyādha pañcabhiḥ sārathiṃ cāsya navabhir icchan bhīṣmasya jīvitam
english: But Sudakṣiṇa, in the battle, pierced the son of Kṛṣṇā's lord with five arrows and his charioteer with nine, wishing to preserve Bhīṣma's life.

sanskrit: tad yuddham āsīt sumahat tayos tatra parākrame yad abhyadhāvad gāṅgeyaṃ śikhaṇḍī śatrutāpanaḥ
english: Mighty was that combat there in their display of prowess, even as Śikhaṇḍin, scorcher of foes, rushed upon the son of Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: virāṭadrupadau vṛddhau vārayantau mahācamūm bhīṣmaṃ ca yudhi saṃrabdhāv ādravantau mahārathau
english: The aged Virāṭa and Drupada, those two great chariot-warriors, holding back the mighty host, in their fury rushed upon Bhīṣma in the battle.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tataḥ kruddhaḥ samāyād rathasattamaḥ tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tava teṣāṃ ca bhārata
english: Then Aśvatthāman, that best of chariot-warriors, came on enraged; and thereupon a battle broke out between your men and theirs, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: virāṭo daśabhir bhallair ājaghāna paraṃtapa yatamānaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ drauṇim āhavaśobhinam
english: Virāṭa, O scorcher of foes, struck with ten broad-headed shafts the son of Droṇa, that mighty archer who shone in battle as he strove.

sanskrit: drupadaś ca tribhir bāṇair vivyādha niśitais tathā guruputraṃ samāsādya bhīṣmasya purataḥ sthitam
english: And Drupada, drawing near, pierced the preceptor's son with three sharp arrows as he stood before Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tatas tau tu vivyādha daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ virāṭadrupadau vṛddhau bhīṣmaṃ prati samudyatau
english: Then Aśvatthāman pierced both of them with ten arrows—the aged Virāṭa and Drupada, who had risen up against Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma vṛddhayoś caritaṃ mahat yad drauṇeḥ sāyakān ghorān pratyavārayatāṃ yudhi
english: There we beheld a marvel, the great feat of those two aged ones, in that they warded off the dreadful arrows of Droṇa's son in the fight.

sanskrit: sahadevaṃ tathā yāntaṃ kṛpaḥ śāradvato 'bhyayāt yathā nāgo vane nāgaṃ matto mattam upādravat
english: As Sahadeva thus came on, Kṛpa, son of Śaradvat, advanced against him, as in the forest a rutting elephant charges another in rut.

sanskrit: kṛpaś ca samare rājan mādrīputraṃ mahāratham ājaghāna śarais tūrṇaṃ saptatyā rukmabhūṣaṇaiḥ
english: And Kṛpa, in the battle, O king, swiftly struck the son of Mādrī, that great chariot-warrior, with seventy gold-decked arrows.

sanskrit: tasya mādrīsutaś cāpaṃ dvidhā ciccheda sāyakaiḥ athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ vivyādha navabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: The son of Mādrī cut his bow in two with his arrows, and then pierced that bowless one with nine shafts.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya samare bhārasādhanam mādrīputraṃ susaṃhṛṣṭo daśabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ ājaghānorasi kruddha icchan bhīṣmasya jīvitam
english: Taking up another bow fit for the heavy work of battle, he, well pleased and enraged, struck the son of Mādrī upon the breast with ten sharpened arrows, wishing to preserve Bhīṣma's life.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavo rājañ śāradvatam amarṣaṇam ājaghānorasi kruddho bhīṣmasya vadhakāṅkṣayā tayor yuddhaṃ samabhavad ghorarūpaṃ bhayāvaham
english: In like manner the Pāṇḍava, O king, enraged, in his desire to slay Bhīṣma, struck the wrathful son of Śaradvat upon the breast; and a combat broke out between the two, dreadful of aspect and terrifying.

sanskrit: nakulaṃ tu raṇe kruddhaṃ vikarṇaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ vivyādha sāyakaiḥ ṣaṣṭyā rakṣan bhīṣmasya jīvitam
english: But Vikarṇa, scorcher of foes, pierced the enraged Nakula in battle with sixty arrows, guarding the life of Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: nakulo 'pi bhṛśaṃ viddhas tava putreṇa dhanvinā vikarṇaṃ saptasaptatyā nirbibheda śilīmukhaiḥ
english: Nakula too, sorely wounded by your bow-wielding son, pierced Vikarṇa with seventy-seven sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tatra tau naraśārdūlau bhīṣmahetoḥ paraṃtapau anyonyaṃ jaghnatur vīrau goṣṭhe govṛṣabhāv iva
english: There those two tigers among men, scorchers of foes, for Bhīṣma's sake, those two heroes smote each other like two bulls in a cattle-pen.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacaṃ raṇe yattaṃ nighnantaṃ tava vāhinīm durmukhaḥ samare prāyād bhīṣmahetoḥ parākramī
english: As Ghaṭotkaca strove in the battle, smiting your host, the valiant Durmukha advanced against him in the fray for Bhīṣma's sake.

sanskrit: haiḍimbas tu tato rājan durmukhaṃ śatrutāpanam ājaghānorasi kruddho navatyā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then the son of Hiḍimbā, O king, enraged, struck Durmukha, scorcher of foes, upon the breast with ninety sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: bhīmasenasutaṃ cāpi durmukhaḥ sumukhaiḥ śaraiḥ ṣaṣṭyā vīro nadan hṛṣṭo vivyādha raṇamūrdhani
english: And Durmukha, that hero, exultant and roaring, pierced the son of Bhīmasena with sixty fair-pointed arrows at the head of the battle.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ raṇe yāntaṃ bhīṣmasya vadhakāṅkṣiṇam hārdikyo vārayām āsa rakṣan bhīṣmasya jīvitam
english: As Dhṛṣṭadyumna came on in the battle, eager to slay Bhīṣma, the son of Hṛdika held him in check, guarding the life of Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: vārṣṇeyaḥ pārṣataṃ śūraṃ viddhvā pañcabhir āyasaiḥ punaḥ pañcāśatā tūrṇam ājaghāna stanāntare
english: The Vṛṣṇi hero, having pierced the brave son of Pṛṣata with five iron arrows, swiftly struck him again upon the breast with fifty more.

sanskrit: tathaiva pārṣato rājan hārdikyaṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha niśitais tīkṣṇaiḥ kaṅkapatraparicchadaiḥ
english: In like manner the son of Pṛṣata, O king, pierced the son of Hṛdika with nine keen, sharp arrows fledged with heron feathers.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ bhīṣmahetor mahāraṇe anyonyātiśayair yuktaṃ yathā vṛtramahendrayoḥ
english: A combat arose between the two in that great battle for Bhīṣma's sake, each striving to surpass the other, as once between Vṛtra and the great Indra.

sanskrit: bhīmasenam athāyāntaṃ bhīṣmaṃ prati mahābalam bhūriśravābhyayāt tūrṇaṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: As mighty Bhīmasena then came on toward Bhīṣma, Bhūriśravas swiftly advanced against him and cried, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: saumadattir atho bhīmam ājaghāna stanāntare nārācena sutīkṣṇena rukmapuṅkhena saṃyuge
english: Then the son of Somadatta struck Bhīma upon the breast in the fray with a very sharp iron shaft fletched with gold.

sanskrit: uraḥsthena babhau tena bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān skandaśaktyā yathā krauñcaḥ purā nṛpatisattama
english: With that shaft lodged in his breast, the valiant Bhīmasena shone, O best of kings, as the Krauñca mountain of old with the spear of Skanda.

sanskrit: tau śarān sūryasaṃkāśān karmāraparimārjitān anyonyasya raṇe kruddhau cikṣipāte muhur muhuḥ
english: The two, enraged, cast at each other again and again in the battle arrows bright as the sun, polished by the smith.

sanskrit: bhīmo bhīṣmavadhākānṣkī saumadattiṃ mahāratham tathā bhīṣmajaye gṛdhnuḥ saumadattiś ca pāṇḍavam kṛtapratikṛte yattau yodhayām āsatū raṇe
english: Bhīma, eager to slay Bhīṣma, and the great chariot-warrior son of Somadatta, greedy for Bhīṣma's victory—each repaying blow with blow, the two fought on intently in the battle.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ mahārāja mahatyā senayā vṛtam bhīṣmāyābhimukhaṃ yāntaṃ bhāradvājo nyavārayat
english: As Yudhiṣṭhira, O great king, surrounded by a mighty host, advanced straight toward Bhīṣma, the son of Bharadvāja held him in check.

sanskrit: droṇasya rathanirghoṣaṃ parjanyaninadopamam śrutvā prabhadrakā rājan samakampanta māriṣa
english: Hearing the roar of Droṇa's chariot, like the thunder of the storm-cloud, the Prabhadrakas, O king, trembled, O honored one.

sanskrit: sā senā mahatī rājan pāṇḍuputrasya saṃyuge droṇena vāritā yattā na cacāla padāt padam
english: That great army of the son of Pāṇḍu, O king, checked in the fray by Droṇa, held firm and stirred not a step from its place.

sanskrit: cekitānaṃ raṇe kruddhaṃ bhīṣmaṃ prati janeśvara citrasenas tava sutaḥ kruddharūpam avārayat
english: As Cekitāna, enraged, advanced against Bhīṣma in the battle, O lord of men, your son Citrasena, terrible in his wrath, held him in check.

sanskrit: bhīṣmahetoḥ parākrāntaś citraseno mahārathaḥ cekitānaṃ paraṃ śaktyā yodhayām āsa bhārata
english: Putting forth his strength for Bhīṣma's sake, the great chariot-warrior Citrasena fought Cekitāna with utmost might, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: tathaiva cekitāno 'pi citrasenam ayodhayat tad yuddham āsīt sumahat tayos tatra parākrame
english: Likewise Cekitāna too fought Citrasena; and mighty indeed was that combat there in their display of prowess.

sanskrit: arjuno vāryamāṇas tu bahuśas tanayena te vimukhīkṛtya putraṃ te tava senāṃ mamarda ha
english: But Arjuna, again and again checked by your son, turned that son of yours away and crushed your army.

sanskrit: duḥśāsano 'pi parayā śaktyā pārtham avārayat kathaṃ bhīṣmaṃ paro hanyād iti niścitya bhārata
english: Duḥśāsana too, with utmost might, held Pārtha in check, resolved that no enemy should slay Bhīṣma, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: sā vadhyamānā samare putrasya tava vāhinī loḍyate rathibhiḥ śreṣṭhais tatra tatraiva bhārata
english: That host of your son, slaughtered in the battle, was churned up here and there by the foremost of chariot-warriors, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca atha vīro maheṣvāso mattavāraṇavikramaḥ samādāya mahac cāpaṃ mattavāraṇavāraṇam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then the heroic mighty archer, with the prowess of a rutting elephant, taking up his great bow that could turn back a rutting elephant—

sanskrit: vidhunvāno dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ drāvayāṇo mahārathān pṛtanāṃ pāṇḍaveyānāṃ pātayāno mahārathaḥ
english: —that great chariot-warrior, brandishing his excellent bow, putting the great chariot-warriors to flight and laying low the army of the Pāṇḍavas—

sanskrit: nimittāni nimittajñaḥ sarvato vīkṣya vīryavān pratapantam anīkāni droṇaḥ putram abhāṣata
english: —Droṇa, valiant and skilled in reading omens, surveying the portents on every side as he scorched the hostile ranks, spoke to his son:

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa divasas tāta yatra pārtho mahārathaḥ jighāṃsuḥ samare bhīṣmaṃ paraṃ yatnaṃ kariṣyati
english: "This is the day, dear son, on which the great chariot-warrior Pārtha, eager to slay Bhīṣma in the battle, will make his utmost effort.

sanskrit: utpatanti hi me bāṇā dhanuḥ prasphuratīva me yogam astrāṇi gacchanti krūre me vartate matiḥ
english: For my arrows leap upward, my bow seems to quiver of itself, my weapons turn ready for use, and my mind dwells upon cruelty.

sanskrit: dikṣu śāntāsu ghorāṇi vyāharanti mṛgadvijāḥ nīcair gṛdhrā nilīyante bhāratānāṃ camūṃ prati
english: Though the quarters are still, beasts and birds cry out fearsomely, and the vultures settle low, facing the army of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: naṣṭaprabha ivādityaḥ sarvato lohitā diśaḥ rasate vyathate bhūmir anuṣṭanati vāhanam
english: The sun seems to have lost its splendor, the quarters are red on every side; the earth resounds and trembles, and the draught-beasts groan.

sanskrit: kaṅkā gṛdhrā balākāś ca vyāharanti muhur muhuḥ śivāś cāśivanirghoṣā vedayantyo mahad bhayam
english: Herons, vultures, and cranes cry out again and again, and jackals with their inauspicious howls portend a great terror.

sanskrit: papāta mahatī colkā madhyenādityamaṇḍalāt sakabandhaś ca parigho bhānum āvṛtya tiṣṭhati
english: A great meteor has fallen through the midst of the sun's orb, and a headless trunk-shaped bar of darkness stands veiling the sun.

sanskrit: pariveṣas tathā ghoraś candrabhāskarayor abhūt vedayāno bhayaṃ ghoraṃ rājñāṃ dehāvakartanam
english: A dreadful halo too has formed about the moon and the sun, portending a fearful terror, the dismembering of the bodies of kings.

sanskrit: devatāyatanasthāś ca kauravendrasya devatāḥ kampante ca hasante ca nṛtyanti ca rudanti ca
english: And the deities set in the shrines of the lord of the Kauravas tremble and laugh and dance and weep.

sanskrit: apasavyaṃ grahāś cakrur alakṣmāṇaṃ niśākaram avākśirāś ca bhagavān udatiṣṭhata candramāḥ
english: The planets have circled the moon, robber of its luster, from the inauspicious side, and the blessed moon has risen with its head turned downward.

sanskrit: vapūṃṣi ca narendrāṇāṃ vigatānīva lakṣaye dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainyeṣu na ca bhrājanti daṃśitāḥ
english: I mark, too, that the bodies of the kings seem drained of luster, and in the armies of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son the mailed warriors shine not.

sanskrit: senayor ubhayoś caiva samantāc chrūyate mahān pāñcajanyasya nirghoṣo gāṇḍīvasya ca nisvanaḥ
english: And throughout both armies on every side is heard the great blast of the Pāñcajanya and the twang of the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: dhruvam āsthāya bībhatsur uttamāstrāṇi saṃyuge apāsyānyān raṇe yodhān abhyasyati pitāmaham
english: Surely, taking his stand and loosing his finest weapons in the fray, Bībhatsu, setting aside the other warriors in the battle, drives straight at the grandsire.

sanskrit: hṛṣyanti romakūpāni sīdatīva ca me manaḥ cintayitvā mahābāho bhīṣmārjunasamāgamam
english: The pores of my skin bristle, and my mind seems to sink, mighty-armed one, as I ponder the meeting of Bhīṣma and Arjuna.

sanskrit: taṃ caiva nikṛtiprajñaṃ pāñcālyaṃ pāpacetasam puraskṛtya raṇe pārtho bhīṣmasyāyodhanaṃ gataḥ
english: Setting before him that Pāñcāla of crooked cunning and evil mind, Pārtha has gone to the battle-ground of Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: abravīc ca purā bhīṣmo nāhaṃ hanyāṃ śikhaṇḍinam strī hy eṣā vihitā dhātrā daivāc ca sa punaḥ pumān
english: And of old Bhīṣma declared: 'I will not slay Śikhaṇḍin, for by the Ordainer this one was fashioned a woman, and only by fate is he now a man.'

sanskrit: amaṅgalyadhvajaś caiva yājñasenir mahārathaḥ na cāmaṅgalaketoḥ sa prahared āpagāsutaḥ
english: The great chariot-warrior, son of Yajñasena, bears an inauspicious standard; and the son of the River-goddess would not strike at one whose emblem is ill-omened.

sanskrit: etad vicintayānasya prajñā sīdati me bhṛśam adyaiva tu raṇe pārthaḥ kuruvṛddham upādravat
english: As I ponder all this, my understanding sinks utterly; for this very day in the battle Pārtha has rushed upon the aged Kuru elder.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasya ca krodho bhīṣmārjunasamāgamaḥ mama cāstrābhisaṃrambhaḥ prajānām aśubhaṃ dhruvam
english: The wrath of Yudhiṣṭhira, the meeting of Bhīṣma and Arjuna, and the fury of my own weapons—surely all this bodes ill for the creatures of the world."
